title: Completeness and the actual completion unit after ordinary open restriction
statement: Fix independent site and coefficient universes, a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, an open immersion j:U→X with ell invertible on residue fields of both schemes, and the section-normalized completed-coefficient open operations o. For every quotient-tower complete unbounded derived object H on X [def-weil-derived-complete], the ordinary exact open restriction j*H is quotient-tower complete on U and the actual normalized completion unit [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] at j*H is invertible. This concerns the given ordinary restriction functor, without choosing a reconstruction equivalence or an arbitrary comparison isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 08TC, 0941, 07A4 and 0G7E; open case of immersion completed-pullback comparison, expanded to the fixed coefficient transports.

proof.text: Use the Roos/intrinsic completeness equivalence and the integral principal-cone local criterion to characterize quotient-tower completeness on any complex representative Q by invertibility of e inverse followed by the specified scalar principal-cone unit. A good representative is needed only for the existing equivalence, not for restricting Q. The coefficient-datum theorem supplies the required principal adic datum; choose an auxiliary prime different from ell.

The completed coefficient map sends the completed uniformizer on X to that on U. Test equality by each limit projection: its projection compatibility reduces this to the finite coefficient map, and finiteConstants gives precisely the required equality of constant residues. Faithfulness of the specified coefficient equivalence, its counit naturality and the equality identifying its functor with ringed pushforward then show that ordinary restriction carries the scalar chain endomorphism to the target scalar endomorphism.

The ordinary adjunction makes restriction preserve countable products. For an additive product-preserving functor, compare the finite principal cones with the cones of their image maps. Their transition and degree-zero inclusion identities give a product isomorphism intertwining one minus the shift and the product augmentation. Mapping the final cocone gives an isomorphism which carries the normalized zero-homotopy unit to the normalized target unit. The private principalMap proof writes this construction directly, reusing the finite-cone and cocone comparison helpers of the exact-equivalence module; no equivalence hypothesis on restriction is used.

Source completeness makes its specified principal-cone unit an isomorphism after derived localization. Naturality of the exact derived-functor comparison shows that localization of its restricted chain map is also an isomorphism. Compose with the principal-completion comparison and the scalar identity from step 2. Apply the arbitrary-representative criterion from step 1 to obtain target completeness, and the Roos/intrinsic equivalence once more to obtain invertibility of the actual normalized completion unit.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A0E principal completion criterion, combined with the normalized Roos equivalence and the product-preserving exact open restriction of Tags 08TC and 0941; fixed-coefficient scalar transport is proved from the given projection and constant-section equations.

lean.statement:
theorem openRestrictionComplete
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ x : U, Invertible (l : U.residueField x)] :
    ∀ H, complete l E X H →
      complete l E U ((star l E j o).obj H) ∧
      IsIso ((IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E U none).app
        ((star l E j o).obj H))
